data.name: Panama
data.summary: Panama has a territorial tax system: foreign dividends, interest and gains on foreign securities are not taxed, and there is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Panamanian-source investment income is taxed lightly (10% on local securities gains, 10%/5% final WHT on local dividends). US/EU withholding taxes on the portfolio are a final cost. The balboa (PAB) is at par with the US dollar, which circulates as legal tender.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (territorial)
regimes.description: Residents and non-residents are taxed only on Panamanian-source income. Foreign dividends, interest and gains on foreign securities are not taxed. Panamanian securities gains 10%; local dividends 10%/5% WHT.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if 183+ days in the current or preceding year, or permanent residence established. Foreign nationals need a residence visa.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on foreign securities are foreign-source and not taxed. Gains on shares, bonds and other securities issued by Panamanian entities: 10% (buyer withholds 5% of price, which the seller may treat as final). Panamanian real estate: 10% of the gain, or the 3% advance on price as final tax.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Panama, Individual - Income determination

open_questions: Exemption for gains on securities registered with the SMV and sold through an organised market (historic Decree-Law 1 of 1999 art. 334) not verified for 2026.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Deloitte Panama Highlights 2026 (updated April 2026); territorial basis. listed_securities_domestic 0.10 ignores a possible exemption for SMV-registered securities sold on an exchange (not verified).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Only Panamanian-source trading income could be taxed (25% corporate / up to 25% personal).

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends are not taxed. Dividends from Panamanian operating companies bear 10% WHT (5% when paid out of foreign-source or exempt income), which is final.
dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte 2026: dividend WHT 10%/5%; 'subsequent distribution not taxed'. Territorial: foreign dividends exempt.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% (Panamanian-source profits) / 5% (foreign-source or exempt profits); 20% for bearer shares; higher retaliatory rates (20%/40%) for discriminating jurisdictions.
dividends.treaty_network: 18 treaties; BEPS MLI in force 1 Mar 2021. No US treaty. As a territorial system, Panama gives no unilateral credit, and US/EU withholding on the family's portfolio is final.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Panama, Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Real estate tax 0%-0.7% for family patrimony/main residence; 0%-1% for other property (Deloitte 2026).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Real estate transfer tax 2% on transfers of Panamanian property (whether it applies to inheritances not checked).

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Panama, Individual - Other taxes

residency.tax_residency_test: 183+ days in the current or preceding calendar year, or permanent residence; centre of economic and family interests relevant (Deloitte 2026).

routes.name: Residence visas (e.g. Qualified Investor, Friendly Nations, Pensionado)
routes.requirements: Panama offers several residence visas; current investment thresholds were not verified in this research.

corporate.summary: Territorial CIT 25% (or 4.67% of gross for large taxpayers, whichever greater); 10% dividend WHT, 5% from foreign-source profits; retained earnings tax.
corporate.special_zones: MHQ regime, Colón Free Zone, Panama Pacifico.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow. Panama levies no tax on the foreign portfolio, so a US family pays full US rates.

Exemption for exchange-traded Panamanian securities not verified.

income.name: Panama

income_tax.summary: Territorial tax on Panamanian-source income: 0% up to USD 11,000, 15% to USD 50,000 and 25% above. Employees pay 9.75% social security plus 1.25% educational insurance with no ceiling.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Deloitte states that contributions of independent contractors and professionals 'may vary from 9% to 13.5%' of fees; the top of that range is shown and the tier for a given income was not verified. Whether educational insurance is added for the self-employed is not stated. Professionals (including independents contracted in Panama) face 15% withholding at source on gross fees (Deloitte).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Territorial: residents and non-residents are taxed only on Panamanian-source income (Deloitte; PwC). Employee rate is CSS 9.75% (from April 2025) plus 1.25% educational insurance (PwC). Deductions include mortgage interest up to USD 15,000, medical insurance and expenses, and USD 800 (married filing jointly); not applied to the brackets. No local income surtax.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Panama, Individual - Taxes on personal income

regimes.name: Short Stay Visa as a Remote Worker (Executive Decree 198 of 2021)
regimes.description: Nine-month stay, extendable once for nine months, for remote workers with a foreign employer or autonomous remote work for clients abroad, earning at least USD 36,000 a year from foreign sources. Holders swear not to work in Panama. The visa itself carries no tax clause: any relief comes from Panama's territorial system (only Panamanian-source income is taxed, Deloitte and PwC 2026), which does not reach pay for work physically performed in Panama, so covers_local_work is false and the regime is not scored as a tax relief.
regimes.duration_note: 9 months plus one 9-month extension. Health insurance for the whole stay is required. A stay beyond 183 days in a calendar year or two makes the person tax resident, which does not change the territorial basis.

sources.title: Kraemer Law: Visa for Remote Workers (Executive Decree 198 of May 7 2021)

open_questions: Kraemer Law does not discuss tax; the 'exempt' treatment follows from Panama's territorial system as described by Deloitte and PwC, not from a visa clause. Neither source defines when remote work done in Panama for a foreign employer is Panamanian-source, so covers_local_work false rests on the general source rule and on there being no statutory exemption; a DGI ruling could change this.
Government fees and the need for a lawyer to file were not verified.
Panama's SEM (multinational headquarters) employee regime is not researched.

income.residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship can use the Short Stay Remote Worker visa (USD 36,000 a year, 9 months + 9 months). Employees of a Panamanian employer need a work permit/visa (not researched). The earlier repo research (data/jurisdictions/PAN.json) lists residence visas (Qualified Investor, Friendly Nations, Pensionado) without verified thresholds. EU, US and other citizens use the same routes. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income; Panama levies no tax on foreign-source income, so there is nothing to credit.
